BC_description: The `.done()` method now causes an irrecoverable fatal error in Node.js environments when an unhandled rejection reaches it. Previously, it might have allowed recovery or silent termination. Now, if a rejection is not handled before `.done()`, the process will exit, which can break applications expecting graceful shutdown or error recovery. This change enforces stricter error handling semantics, aligning with best practices for unhandled rejection management in modern Node.js.
Adaptation_method: Ensure all promises are properly handled before calling `.done()`. Example: Before - `promise.done();` without full error handling; After - must fully handle rejections: `promise.catch(handleError).done();`. Use `.done()` only as a final terminator after all error handling to prevent unhandled rejections from reaching `.done()`.
